Commentary.Commentary: We are back. The players are out in the middle. Aryan Dutt to bowl first.
...THE CHASE...

Scotland won't be that disappointed too as they pulled things back in the last two overs or so. However, they were not up to the mark with the ball on most occasions. A couple of gentle full toss were hit away while they dropped a couple of catches too. They were constantly put under pressure on the field and were made to do some misfield. The spinners had control of the game. Watt, Main bowled really well. Leask too was economical. Now then! Not a big score but it's not easy to bat as well. Scotland will be under pressure as Netherlands bowlers now know who the pitch is playing. Can their bowlers defend this down? Let's find out.

A fine performance from Netherlands and they have finished with a par score on a pitch which looks like two-paced. Netherlands were told to bat first and the openers laid a wonderful foundation. Max O'Dowd and Michael Levitt added 68 runs. Both played with intent and Netherlands were looking for a score around 180 but they lost a bit of momentum as wickets started falling. Vikramjit Singh played a quick cameo in the middle phase but the hosts lacked someone who could have given them a grand stand finish.
Two runs to end the innings. Full and on middle, Doram works it to deep mid-wicket for a couple. Netherlands end with 167/8.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the game to begin. The two umpires make their way out to the middle as do the players of Scotland. It will be Michael Levitt and Max O'Dowd to open the innings for the Netherlands. Bradley Currie will start with the new ball for Scotland. Away we go...

The captain of the Netherlands, Scott Edwards says that they would have bowled first as well. States that they have played a fair bit of cricket here so they are comfortable doing both. Tells that it is about taking one game at a time and hit the ground running at the World Cup. Informs that Daniel Doram makes his debut. Mentions that they will assess in the Powerplay what a good score is and take it from there.
Scotland's skipper, Richie Berrington says that they will bowl first as it looks like a good wicket. Adds this series will help to prepare for the World Cup, they want to adapt quickly and play well.
Scotland (Playing XI) - Michael Jones, Ollie Hairs, Charlie Tear, Richie Berrington (C), Matthew Cross (WK), Michael Leask, Mark Watt, Chris Greaves, Chris Sole, Gavin Main, Bradley Currie.

Netherlands (Playing XI) - Max O'Dowd, Michael Levitt, Vikramjit Singh, Scott Edwards (C/WK), Sybrand Engelbrecht, Teja Nidamanuru, Logan van Beek, Paul van Meekeren, Daniel Doram (On T20I debut), Aryan Dutt, Vivian Kingma.
TOSS - Scotland have won the toss and they have opted to BOWL first.

Scotland have had the better of Netherlands in the recent past but are lacking some international match time. However, this series is perfect for both teams actually to try and test their strategies before lighting up the World Cup. Netherlands recently played a tri-series against Nepal and Namibia, they looked quite sharp in the series but this probably is a ladder up as Scotland and Ireland have more international experience and will be a perfect match-up just before the main event. Let's hope we get some entertainment from both sides. Stay tuned for toss and other updates.

A triangular series is a rarity nowadays in international cricket, you don't often see it much but we finally have one as Netherlands are all set to host Ireland and Scotland for six T20I matches just before the World Cup kicks off. We welcome you all for the action between Netherlands and Scotland.
...MATCH DAY...

With the T20 World Cup 2024 looming large on the horizon, the Netherlands, Scotland and Ireland are all geared up to compete in a T20I Tri-Series as part of their preparation for the tournament. This series will see the three European teams face each other in a round-robin format, with each team playing against the others twice, but no final match will be played. Ireland, having just completed a packed schedule with an all-format tour against Afghanistan followed by a three-match T20 series against Pakistan, will have had ample game time to fine-tune their squad. In contrast, the Netherlands and Scotland will need to use this series to get their strategies right and ensure they enter the World Cup as well-oiled machines. The series kicks off with the Netherlands and Scotland locking horns in the first match at the Voorburg Cricket Club in The Hague, setting the stage for an action-packed and highly anticipated competition. Scotland have had a slight advantage over the Netherlands, winning three out of their last five encounters, which adds an extra layer of intensity to this battle. The Netherlands, however, come into this series riding high on the momentum of their recent Tri-Series win against Nepal and Namibia, a success they will look to build upon. Led by Scott Edwards, the team boasts a balanced batting lineup that blends experience with youthful exuberance. Key players like Michael Levitt and Sybrand Engelbrecht, alongside the seasoned Max O'Dowd, are expected to be pivotal with the bat. The bowling department appears well-rounded, featuring the likes of Paul van Meekeren, Vivian Kingma and Logan van Beek. Scotland, on the other hand, come into the series with a balanced side led by Richie Berrington who also leads the batting unit featuring George Munsey and Brandon McMullen which promises to be formidable. The bowling unit, comprising Mark Watt, Bradley Currie and Jack Jarvis could prove to be a potent force. Additionally, Scotland's lineup boasts several all-rounders, adding depth and versatility to the team. With both teams eager to start strong and set the tone for an enticing series, the intensity is soaring high. Will the Netherlands carry their momentum forward, or will Scotland leverage their recent success to claim the first win? We shall soon find out!
